prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original SNES pixel-art DEMOLITION HAMMER weapon atlas for Sean in side-scrolling plumbing action game. Oversized heavy rectangular STEEL sledgehammer head with worn bright edges, sturdy dark shaft and ORANGE rubber grip, chunky dark navy outlines, clear pixel clusters. Exactly 3 columns x 3 rows of equal cells, transparent square canvas. No person or hands. Row1: diagonal inventory icon full hammer; held ready hammer diagonal up-right; windup hammer raised overhead to left. Row2: strike hammer slamming down-right head leading; follow-through hammer low diagonal right; isolated broad pale orange swing arc. Row3: small orange-white ground contact star with gray debris; large low radial impact shockwave with stone chips; settling gray dust and chips. All full tool sprites same scale and same lower grip pivot position within cell. Keep head/shaft/grip identical in all poses. Big weighty overhead-slam impression. All 9 sprites entirely inside separate cells with wide margins; no overlapping edges, no clipping. Transparent zero-alpha backdrop, opaque sprite interiors, no atmospheric haze, no ground plane, no text labels grids or UI.

integration_notes: Source sheet is visually reviewed, not a validated runtime atlas.
Generated sprites can cross nominal cell edges; inspect and isolate regions before import.
Measure per-frame grip pivots and muzzle sockets; preserve one weapon scale across held poses.
Do not fit every frame to its opaque bounds; that changes tool scale and grip alignment.
Existing character sheets include baked-in weapons. Clean hand/body layers are needed before attaching these tools.
Mirror held sprites for left-facing play; effects should use their contact or muzzle origin.
Visual effects do not define collision, damage, reach, travel distance, or blast radius.
Clean alpha fringes and validate readable icons and effects at gameplay size.
Strike/follow-through include baked-in arc/debris; avoid double-drawing standalone effects.
